Unlike existing solutions, SprintForge prioritizes agile sprint planning, enterprise security, and multi-user collaboration with Excel as the source of truth.

Hey, I'm Frank Bria 👋

I build AI systems and help investors understand them.

By day: Principal Product Consultant at American Express, working on data governance and GL reconciliation at scale.

By night: Building in the AI tooling space. My ralph-claude-code project (autonomous agentic coding loops) has 6k+ stars and taught me more about where AI development is actually heading than any whitepaper.

In a past life: Founder/Co-Founder of Fintech startups. One of the creators of banking pricing optimization technology. Industry analyst at Tower Group (now Gartner), where I spent years telling banks what analytics/ML/AI technology actually mattered and telling vendors what banks actually needed. Author of Seven Billion Banks on personalized banking.

What I'm Working On

  • ralph-claude-code — Autonomous AI development framework with intelligent exit detection, rate limiting, and safety guardrails. The most-starred implementation in the agentic coding space.
  • CodeFRAME — Next-gen multi-agent coding environment. AI swarms that plan, build, test, and deploy.
  • SprintForge — Project management with Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic timeline predictions.

The Other Stuff

I'm also a mathematician (algebraic topology, K-theory), a composer for film and media, and I speak German fluently plus enough Russian, French, and Italian to get into trouble.

I host The 6 to 7 Figures Show podcast and occasionally write about scaling consulting practices.

Let's Talk

I do advisory work on AI infrastructure strategy and technical due diligence through BSG (Bria Strategy Group).

    Supports DLMS/Cosem IEC IEC 62056-21 Mode E (Hdlc), session mode and passive PUSH mode readout. Подключение EspHome к счетчикам электроэнергии по протоколу СПОДЭС ГОСТ Р 58940-202 (Энергомера ce207, ce208, CE307, CE308, Меркурий, Пульсар, Милур, Мир, Нартис, РиМ и другие).

Hi, I'm Anton 👋

Embedded & IoT engineer — energy metering · CAN bus · reverse engineering · ESPHome

I build firmware and tools that live at the boundary between hardware and software: reading electricity & water meters, sniffing automotive CAN buses, and reverse-engineering embedded devices. Most of my open work ships as ESPHome components for utility meters, plus the protocol libraries underneath them. When I'm not on a serial bus, I'm designing PCBs in KiCad.

⭐ Highlights

Project ★ What it is
arduino-canbus-monitor 336 CAN bus monitor on Arduino implementing the Lawicel SLCAN ASCII protocol (CAN232/CANUSB compatible).
tenda-reverse 156 Reverse engineering & root access for the Tenda MW6 WiFi mesh router (RTL8197F).
esphome-energomera-iec 40 ESPHome component for Energomera CE102M/CE301/CE303/CE307 (IEC 61107) meters.
esphome-dlms-cosem 39 ESPHome ↔ DLMS/COSEM (IEC 62056-21 Mode E / СПОДЭС) electricity meters.
jeep-canbus 30 CAN bus projects for Chrysler/Jeep — VES enabler and other hacks.
painlessMeshMqttGateway 27 MQTT ↔ painlessMesh gateway bridging an IoT mesh to Ethernet.

🧩 ESPHome — Core Contributions

I'm an active contributor to the official ESPHome project, where I've authored and maintain a number of sensor, display, and accelerometer components that now ship with ESPHome itself. (merged PRs · all PRs)

Components I authored (merged into ESPHome core):

…plus fixes & enhancements to LTR390, INA226, VEML7700, BME280, the ac_dimmer (ESP-IDF 5+), and the i2c bus.

I'm also one of the main developers of esphome-libs/dlms_parser — the shared DLMS/COSEM parsing library used across the ESPHome ecosystem, which grew out of my own esphome-dlms-cosem work.

In progress (open PRs): AS7341 / AS7343 spectral sensors, HUSB238 USB-PD controller, ST LIS2DH12 & LIS2DW12 accelerometers, Waveshare CH32V003 I/O expander, CST328 touch controller, BH1745 colour sensor, and signal filters.

Hej there 👋

I'm Konrad, web developer from Dresden 🇩🇪 with a main focus on PHP development, especially for 🧡 TYPO3 projects. I love open source, enjoy working in collaborative environments and continuously strive to improve my skills and code quality through learning and feedback.

🧡 TYPO3 Extensions

  • EXT:ai_mate – A symfony/ai-mate bridge for TYPO3 that serves resolved runtime facts to AI assistants via MCP.
  • EXT:content_planner – Page status functionality to support the planning of content work, e.g. a migration process.
  • EXT:dump_server – Brings the Symfony Var Dump Server to TYPO3.
  • EXT:environment_indicator – Several features to show an environment indicator in the frontend and backend.
  • EXT:file_sync – Synchronize missing files between TYPO3 instances.
  • EXT:frontend_edit – Provides an edit button for editors within frontend content elements.
  • EXT:image_compression – Compress automatically images within the TYPO3 backend.
  • EXT:internal_news – Provides an internal news system for the TYPO3 backend.
  • EXT:letter_avatar – Generates colorful backend user avatars using name initials letter.
  • EXT:login_warning – Extends the TYPO3 backend login warning_mode functionality to inform about suspicious logins.
  • EXT:pagetree_facets – Filterable TYPO3 page tree with an extensible filter tab API.
  • EXT:request_profiler – Lightweight dev-only request profiler for TYPO3 — surfaces N+1 queries, cache misses and slow pages as AI-readable JSON.
  • EXT:routing – Register frontend endpoints via PHP attributes on controller methods — an attribute-based alternative to AjaxRoutes.php.
  • EXT:routing_mcp – MCP tools for TYPO3 frontend routes — expose #[Route] endpoints to AI agents with #[McpTool].
  • EXT:solr_dashboard_widgets – A set of useful TYPO3 Solr dashboard widgets.
  • EXT:styleguide – TYPO3 extension with several tools for a simple styleguide.

📦 PHP Libraries

  • move-elevator/composer-translation-validator – Validates translation files in your project.
  • move-elevator/deployer-tools – The Deployer Tools combine multiple deployer recipes for an improved deployment process and workflow.
  • php-color – Tiny, dependency-free PHP library for color conversion, contrast and string-to-color hashing.
  • php-doc-block-header-fixer – PHP CS Fixer rule to fix the class header regarding PHP DocBlocks.
  • php-progress – Modern, dependency-free CLI progress bars & spinners for PHP.
  • php-sync-tool – PHP database & file sync over SSH/rsync/SFTP with CMS framework auto-detection.
  • ttt – Declarative test sandboxing for TYPO3 via PHP attributes.

🖥️ Apps

  • beacon – Lightweight macOS menu bar app that brings GitHub and GitLab notifications into one place.
  • canopy – Jira companion that visualizes issues in a hierarchical tree view with filtering, grouping and real-time change tracking.
  • clockwork/ai – Simple DIY clock project to generate AI poems by current time.
  • devcap-app – Native macOS menubar companion to devcap, showing daily git commits at a glance.
  • roots – Desktop app that aggregates work time from multiple services (Moco, Jira, Outlook, Personio) into a unified timeline.
  • spark – Native macOS menu bar app that shows your Claude Code usage at a glance.

⚡ Developer Tools

  • devcap – CLI tool that aggregates git commits across multiple local repositories for daily stand-ups and time tracking.
  • md-annotator – AI coding agent plugin that opens Markdown files in a browser-based annotator for review and feedback.

🛠️ DevOps

  • db_sync_tool – Python script to synchronize a database from an origin to a target system.
  • ddev-typo3-multi-version-extension – DDEV add-on for TYPO3 multi version instances for TYPO3 extension development.

🎨 Resources

  • Weather Iconic – An open source weather icon set.

📫 Contact: hej@konradmichalik.dev

Hi there 👋

I'm Stan, a software engineer interested in all parts of the stack, from low-level system programming and infra to web development and mobile apps.

I love building and contributing to open-source projects in my free time. I also maintain a curated list of my starred projects.

Projects

Web 🌐

  • Larafeed: A web-based feed reader for following and organizing RSS feeds.
  • Bulla: A commenting system for static websites and blogs.
  • Gongyu: A bookmark manager inspired by Shaarli.
  • Pastekey: Passkey-only, end-to-end encrypted text and file sharing.
  • Meridian: Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted Obsidian sync.
  • Enedis: A live, street-level map of power outages reported by Enedis in France.
  • Koliko: Privacy-first usage analytics for coding agents.
  • Mullvad Relay Map: An interactive map of Mullvad VPN relays with latency estimates.
  • Vélib Pulse: A map-first view of Vélib’ Métropole availability in Paris.

These days, I like to use Cloudflare Workers, React, and Effect.

Mobile 📱

  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding agent with a native iOS client built in SwiftUI.
  • firstfm-ios: iOS client for Last.fm written with Swift and SwiftUI.

Desktop 🖥️

  • Qhostty: An experimental native Qt 6 frontend for Ghostty, built for KDE Plasma on Linux.
  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding agent with a native macOS client built in SwiftUI.
  • MacThrottle: A macOS menu bar app for monitoring thermal throttling, built with SwiftUI.

Terminal 💻

  • ncda: An ncdu-like Linux TUI for monitoring live file I/O with eBPF, built with Rust, Aya, and Ratatui.
  • fast-resume: A full-text search TUI for finding and resuming coding sessions, built with Rust, Ratatui, and Tantivy.
  • pi-extensions: A collection of TypeScript extensions for the Pi coding agent, including UI, workflow, and quality-of-life features.
  • hue-tui: A TUI to control Philips Hue lights, built with Go and Bubble Tea.
  • opencode-wakatime: An OpenCode plugin written in TypeScript to track code activity in WakaTime.
  • noclaw: A tiny autonomous AI assistant written in C, shipping as a single binary with a 324 KB memory footprint. (for the meme)

Systems and sandboxing 📦

  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding environment with sessions isolated in Kata Containers microVMs using Cloud Hypervisor.
  • Codebench: Code benchmarking platform with Go workers running inside Firecracker microVMs.
  • krowl: A distributed web crawler in Go with durable local storage, consistent-hash sharding, and WARC capture.

Home automation 🏡

  • teleinfo2mqtt-rs: Convert TeleInfo frames from a Linky meter's serial port to Home Assistant-compatible MQTT messages. I also built my own MQTT client for this.
  • hue-tui: A TUI to control Philips Hue lights, built with Go and Bubble Tea.
  • lametric-time: A Linux toolkit for recovering and provisioning a LaMetric TIME through its undocumented setup API.

Infrastructure 🔁

  • wireguard-install: WireGuard VPN installer for Linux servers.
  • openvpn-install: OpenVPN installer for Linux servers.
  • nginx-autoinstall: Compile NGINX from source with custom modules and patches on Debian and Ubuntu.
  • ansible-roles: My Ansible roles for Debian and Ubuntu.
  • awesome-lxc-lxd: A curated list of awesome LXC and LXD tools, libraries, and related projects.
  • nixos-config: My NixOS configuration files.
  • arch-linux-install: My Arch Linux installation notes.
More projects
Web and tools
  • matomo-to-umami: A Python tool to migrate analytics data from Matomo (MySQL) to Umami (PostgreSQL).
  • trakt-cli: A CLI tool for trakt.tv in Go.
  • codex-wakatime: A Codex CLI plugin written in TypeScript to track code activity in WakaTime.
Infrastructure and configuration
  • feedbin-docker: Self-host your own Feedbin RSS reader in Docker.
  • docker-pleroma: Docker image for the Pleroma federated social network.
Earlier projects

  • palette: Extract color palette from an image with k-means and k-NN (OpenCV, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy).
  • Soundhive: Music sharing service (NestJS, Angular, JavaFX, audio fingerprint in C++).

Dr Alexander Mikhalev

United Kingdom · Systems thinker · Founder of Terraphim & Applied Knowledge Systems

Building privacy-preserving AI that works for the user — and the agent tooling that ships it.

Local-First AI · Knowledge Graphs · Agentic Engineering · Digital Twins · Systems Engineering · Rust

Terraphim · Open Source · Writing · Recognition · Connect · Background

Terraphim

Terraphim is a privacy-preserving AI assistant: a local-first knowledge graph search engine built in Rust and WebAssembly. Sub-millisecond Aho-Corasick pattern matching over role-based knowledge graphs — on your hardware, with zero telemetry, no account, and no cloud dependency. Ships as CLI, desktop app, HTTP server, MCP server, and browser extension, with native hooks for AI coding assistants.

Website · Docs · Origin Story · Forum

Open Source Highlights

Terraphim AI — the privacy-preserving AI assistant

Local-first knowledge graph search engine in Rust and WebAssembly: sub-millisecond Aho-Corasick matching over role-based knowledge graphs, zero telemetry, no account. Ships as CLI, Tauri desktop app, HTTP server, MCP server, and WASM browser extension — 52+ workspace crates.

Reference Architecture for AI — patterns for production agent systems

The harness, not the model, determines agent success — +26% benchmark gain (52.8 → 66.5% on Terminal Bench 2.0) with zero model changes. Context architecture, execution guardrails, and memory infrastructure that actually works. Organisation: reference-architecture-ai (site source) · Medium publication.

Terraphim Agents Forge — Gitea fork for AI agent-native development

Gitea fork extended for the agent economy: PageRank-powered issue triage, dependency graphs, native MCP server, and scoped robot accounts with full audit trails. Upstream-compatible — runs our fleet at git.terraphim.cloud.

terraphim-skills.md — production-grade skills for AI agents

57 curated, battle-tested, cryptographically signed skills for Claude Code, Codex, and other agent CLIs — disciplined engineering, Rust performance, DevOps, orchestration. One-command verified install: cargo install terraphim-skills → tsm install <skill>.

Terraphim Forge — the code forge built for AI agents

Pay-first SaaS that hands each customer their own Gitea-on-Firecracker microVM within ~30 seconds of checkout — container, npm, and Cargo registries included. Public demo (resets daily): demo.terraphim-forge.com.

Synth — declarative synthetic data generation

The Declarative Data Generator: realistic, constraint-based synthetic data from schema-as-code — database agnostic, scales to millions of rows, version-controlled and peer-reviewable like any other code. Fork carrying the getsynth/synth lineage (★1.4k upstream) forward. Companion content: synth-data-engineering.

Plus the entire Terraphim organisation — 66 public repositories, 52+ Rust workspace crates.

Writing

  • metacortex.engineer — long-form engineering notes
  • Terraphim origin story — from The Pattern (Redis Hackathon Platinum winner) through Kaggle and Oxford to Terraphim AI
  • INCOSE EMEA webinar — semantic search over the systems engineering body of knowledge

Recognition

  • Platinum winner, Redis "Build on Redis" Hackathon 2021 — real-time NLP for medical literature (The Pattern)
  • Innovate UK funded — talent digital shadow, project "ATOMIC" (TSB Project No: 600594)
  • Digital twin programmes for Boeing and Rolls-Royce aircraft networks
  • Speaker, INCOSE EMEA — semantic search and systems engineering

Connect

Background

  • Founder, Applied Knowledge Systems Ltd — applied AI, digital twins, sensor fusion
  • AI lead architect at Nationwide; CTO & Head of AI at Zestic AI — taking innovation from idea to production (metacortex.engineer)
  • The Pattern — Redis Hackathon Platinum Winner: outperformed Nvidia's ML pipeline for BERT QA inference on CPU; results presented at a public lecture at Oxford University, Green Templeton College (origin story)
  • Methodology validated in the INCOSE community for the Systems Engineering Handbook v.4 — a recognised low-effort substitution for formal model-based systems engineering
  • Systems engineering: operational digital twins of aircraft networks for Boeing and Rolls-Royce
  • IoT sensor fusion: LiDAR and acoustic-based water-flow monitoring
  • Building with knowledge graphs since the CORD-19 era; local-first AI full-time since 2022
  • The name Terraphim comes from the Relict series of science fiction novels by Vasiliy Golovachev — an artificial intelligence living inside a spacesuit (part of an exocortex), designed to help you with your tasks

👋 Hi, I'm Anand

Anand Chowdhary is a technology entrepreneur, engineer, designer, and GitHub Star.

He is Head of Product of Sycamore, the trusted agent operating system for the enterprise, backed by a $65 million seed round.

Previously, he built FirstQuadrant, an all-in-one AI sales platform funded by Y Combinator. He also makes angel investments and does some nonprofit work on the side.

Learn more on anandchowdhary.com →

README — A guide to work with me

Pronounciation

/ɑnʌnð t͡ʃŏɖʱɹi/ (similar to Aah-nun'd Cho-dree).

About me

  • I made my first website and published it to the web when I was ten years old. I'm 28.80 now.
  • I'm from New Delhi and have lived in Enschede, Groningen, San Francisco, and now Utrecht.
  • I track all my habits, travel, and biomarkers, and they have an API (yes, really).
  • Apart from my day (+night) job, I also advise early-stage startups and contribute to open source projects.

Quirks

  • When in long meetings, I tend to get distracted and often find myself ⌘+↹-ing to a different window (I used to previously catch myself using my phone, so I keep it away from me now). I'm working on this but please call me out if you notice I'm not paying attention.
  • I typically work long hours, so you might receive an email or Slack message from me at unholy hours; you don't have to read or reply immediately if you're not working, and I don't expect you to work at the same times.
  • I'm still learning how to transition from designer/developer/hacker/etc. to manager, so you'll likely have to bare with my lack of discipline when it comes to important managerial responsibilities like setting up projects well in advance and providing useful feedback.
  • I tend to think and talk fast, so I might jump in while someone is still talking and try to finish their thought. This is also something I'm working on, so if you say "Let me finish", it'll make me feel like I'm a prick and make me much more conscious of this.
  • My co-founder Carlo told me that I am "very good at things [I] want to do, and so bad at things I don't want to do". I want to do a better job at tasks that are important, but those I'm not particular excited about.

What I value & how you can help me

  • Keeping things in the open: Just like this README, I keep my OKRs, life and health data, and everything else I can, public. If it's not public, it's shared internally with the team (e.g., my calendar, Pabio finance details, and life updates). I value transparency, even in the little things like posting in Slack channels rather than direct messages.
  • Feed me back: I ask for feedback. If we have a one-on-one meeting, I highly value receiving feedback on how I can improve personally, do my job better, or help you do your job better. This also applies to my personal relationships.
